title: Money: Naira Notes, Adding, Change and Shopping
seo_title: Money – Primary 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Recognise naira notes from ₦5 to ₦1,000; add and subtract amounts of money; give change; multiply simple amounts of money. (summary of the NERDC Primary 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 3 maths worksheets on Nigerian money: naira notes from ₦5 to ₦1,000, counting money, adding prices, giving change and buying more than one item. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Nigerian money is the naira (₦). Notes include ₦5, ₦10, ₦20, ₦50, ₦100, ₦200, ₦500 and ₦1,000.
  • To count money, start with the note of the highest value and count on.
  • Change is the money you get back: money paid − price.

Examples

Example

₦200 + ₦100 + ₦50 + ₦20

Count on from ₦200

Answer: ₦370

Example

Pay ₦500 for a ₦350 book

500 − 350

Answer: ₦150 change

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting notes instead of their valuesThree notes can be worth more than five notes.
Adding when finding changeChange = paid − price.
Forgetting the ₦ signAlways write ₦.

Why should we check our change?
faq.a: To make sure we get the right money back.
